principles.statement: One idea per sentence, one topic per paragraph — complexity belongs in the structure, not the sentences.
principles.rationale: Readers parse technical content serially; a sentence carrying two ideas loses one of them.

principles.statement: Prefer concrete nouns and active verbs; delete intensifiers.
principles.rationale: 'The parser validates tokens' beats 'the parser effectively and efficiently performs validation of tokens'.

principles.statement: Define a term before or immediately after first use — and use it consistently thereafter.
principles.rationale: Synonym variation (id/identifier/reference for one thing) forces readers to guess whether the differences are meaningful.

heuristics.name: Read it aloud
heuristics.description: Sentences you can't say in one breath lose readers; run-ons and buried clauses become audible.
examples: A 45-word sentence with three nested clauses reads as three sentences.

heuristics.name: Example-to-abstraction ratio
heuristics.description: Every abstraction earns its place only if a concrete example follows within a paragraph.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Any section introducing a new concept.
examples: 'Idempotency' explained twice without one 'run it twice, same result' example fails.

decision_rules.condition: A paragraph can be deleted without losing information the reader needs.
decision_rules.action: Delete it — length is not rigor.

decision_rules.condition: The same fact is stated in two places in the same doc.
decision_rules.action: State it once at the authoritative location and reference it — duplicated facts drift.
